summary: Lower instance field initializers that reference this into explicit constructor-time statements at the JavaScript-defined point.

target.notes: Do not use a C# field initializer. Inject an assignment into the generated constructor at the JS field-initialization point so `this` is available and ordering is preserved.

semantics.base_class: initializer runs before base constructor body
semantics.method_dispatch: this may call methods already present on the prototype

caveats: C# instance field initializers cannot generally model JavaScript `this` use or derived ordering; constructor injection is required.

tests.name: initializer uses another earlier field
tests.input: class C { a=2; b=this.a+1; } console.log(new C().b);

tests.name: edge: textual order matters
tests.input: class C { b=this.a; a=2; } console.log(new C().b);
tests.expected_behavior: b observes undefined because a is not initialized yet
